title: The Playlist of Route 9
premise: Astrid Delacroix, a scholarship student at Ashgrove Academy, survives on a strict playlist and a countdown to graduation — until her music teacher pairs her with Theo Marchetti, the boy whose family destroyed hers, for a semester-long project restoring the school's forgotten radio station. Digging through old broadcasts, they uncover evidence that the academy's beloved founder covered up a student's death decades ago, a cover-up Astrid's own mother was silenced over. As Astrid and Theo's uneasy alliance deepens into something neither expected, they must win the regional broadcast championship to get their findings on air before graduation — knowing that exposing the truth will cost Astrid her scholarship, her future, and possibly each other. In the end, she chooses justice over survival, broadcasting the truth at the championship finale and walking out of Ashgrove with nothing but the truth, a new family of misfits, and Theo's hand in hers.
about_author: Jude Voss is the pen name of a former small-town radio DJ who spent three years teaching music in underfunded schools before turning to fiction. They write stories about kids who find their voices in the static between what they're told and what's true.

chapters.title: Day 214
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She counts down the days to graduation while navigating Ashgrove's class divide, her scholarship precarity, and her headphones-anchored routine. When her mother's old cassette falls from a box, Astrid hears a fragment of a broadcast that makes her mother go pale. Beat: restless longing for escape.

chapters.title: Assigned Seats
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Music teacher Ms. Okonkwo announces semester pairs for restoring the defunct campus radio station, WASH — and assigns Astrid with Theo Marchetti, heir to the Delacroix family's ruin. Their first meeting is all barbed politeness. Beat: fury and dread at being trapped together.

chapters.title: Static and Dust
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He reveals he requested the pairing — he needs Astrid's technical genius and suspects his own family's name is tangled in the station's shutdown. In the studio basement they find equipment still warm, as if someone's been using it. Beat: reluctant curiosity overriding hatred.

chapters.title: The Rules of Survival
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Flashbacks weave through her first year at Ashgrove: the scholarship terms, the unspoken code that poor kids stay invisible. Her best friend Priya warns her that digging into school history is how students disappear from rosters. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: Track One
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Restoring the transmitter, they play a salvaged reel: a girl's voice, 1998, signing off mid-broadcast. Astrid recognizes the cadence — it's her mother. Neither says so aloud. Beat: the past cracking open the present.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Ms. Okonkwo enters WASH in the regional high school broadcast championship — a joke contest nobody respects. But winning grants a live, uncensored final broadcast. Astrid realizes the stage is also a weapon. Beat: scheming hope.

chapters.title: Enemies, Apparently
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Late-night work sessions turn almost easy; he admits his father ordered the station sealed after 'an incident.' A near-moment of connection is interrupted by headmaster Whitlock's inspection, cold and pointed. Beat: warmth shadowed by surveillance.

chapters.title: What Mama Buried
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She confronts her mother, who admits she attended Ashgrove on scholarship in the nineties and knew the dead girl — Lena Okafor — whose death was ruled an accident. Her mother begs her to let it lie. Beat: betrayal and grief.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Someone ransacks the studio; the recovered tapes are gone except one hidden in Astrid's bag. Theo's father summons him home and delivers an ultimatum: quit the project or lose everything. Beat: pressure closing in from both families.

chapters.title: The Misfit Frequency
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Priya, studio tech Marcus, and quiet archivist June join the cause — a found-family crew broadcasting test signals across campus at night. For one night, Astrid feels belonging instead of survival. Beat: joy, fragile and stolen.

chapters.title: Lena's Voice
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The surviving tape reveals Lena investigating the founder's embezzlement days before her death — and naming Theo's grandfather as a witness who stayed silent. Theo must choose his legacy or the truth. Beat: identity shaken to the foundation.

chapters.title: Detention
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Whitlock detains Astrid on fabricated vandalism charges, offering a deal: drop the project, keep the scholarship. Alone in the office, she sees Lena's photo still hanging, mislabeled. Beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Two Championships
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo publicly refuses his father, burning his inheritance bridge, and tells Astrid they're going to win both championships — the broadcast one, and the one for Lena's memory. Beat: alliance becomes devotion.

chapters.title: Signal Lost
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Sabotage kills the transmitter days before regionals; suspicion fractures the crew when evidence points to Marcus. Astrid's faith wavers as Whitlock dangles expulsion. Beat: despair and doubt.

chapters.title: The Confession Tape
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. June finds Lena's final diary in the archive: she recorded the founder's confession the night she died, and the tape was never destroyed — it's been in the station's 'dead air' archive all along. Beat: electrifying hope.

chapters.title: Marcus
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Marcus confesses — Whitlock blackmailed him over his immigration status. Instead of exile, the crew forgives him and turns him double agent inside the administration. Beat: mercy as strength; trust rebuilt.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for the End
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Quiet interlude: repairs done, the crew runs a full rehearsal. Astrid and Theo finally speak plainly about what happens after graduation — different cities, different lives. An almost-kiss, interrupted by the transmitter humming alive on its own. Beat: tenderness on a countdown.

chapters.title: Whitlock's Counterplay
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Whitlock revokes Astrid's scholarship effective immediately and has security waiting to remove her before the championship. Her mother arrives unexpectedly — and hands Astrid the missing tapes she'd hidden for twenty-five years. Beat: generational courage passed on.

chapters.title: On Air
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Championship day. The crew smuggles Astrid in through the radio room; as judges score their showcase segment, Theo stalls on-air while Marcus patches the archive feed. Beat: breathless, ticking-clock tension.

chapters.title: Dead Air No More
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Climax. Astrid takes the mic and broadcasts Lena's confession tape live across the region — the founder's voice admitting everything. Whitlock lunges for the cutoff switch; the crew forms a human wall around the console until the broadcast completes. Beat: triumphant, terrifying truth-telling.

chapters.title: After the Static Clears
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Fallout: the founder's estate is investigated, Whitlock resigns, and Lena's case is reopened. Astrid loses the scholarship but wins a journalism fellowship funded by listeners who heard the broadcast. Beat: grief and vindication entwined.

chapters.title: Track Twenty-Two
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Graduation day. Astrid walks the stage to polite applause and walks out to real cheers — Priya, Marcus, June, her mother, Theo. At the station, she signs off WASH's final broadcast with her own voice, then signs on its next one. Beat: belonging earned, future begun.
